reviewers.persona: Kursleiterin DaF (A1.1): Natürlichkeit, Niveau, Didaktik, Szenenplausibilität

method: Every German string was read. Every item (start gist, 3 × 5 inputItems, 3 × 4 structuredInput, 3 × 11 pool items, 3 × 4 reserve, 10 exam items, 8 check items, 4 proof items) was solved blind from promptDe plus options/tiles/audio line, using the compiler's rendered form for sentence_building (SCHEMA §3.1: 'Bilden Sie den Satz: [tiles]') and check.js, which folds . , ! ? before comparing (src/lib/lesson/check.js l. 42/158), so a final '?' in the key cannot tell a question from a statement. Exam blocks were checked against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json (h1, h2, sp3, s2) and rubrics sd1-sp3 / sd1-s2; exam-text word counts were recounted. The grammar ceiling was checked against grammar-spine.json (g.akkusativ productive a1.1-u06, chunk from u04; g.praep-dativ chunk from u05; g.imperativ-du-ihr a1.2-u09), the rule cards against a1.1/rule-cards.json, new-word load against level-profiles.json (a1.1: 24–32 new per unit; 32 here), can-dos against registries/cando/a1.json, cast facts against casts/series.json and casts/a1.json, and the unit against curriculum/a1-1.md §4. All arithmetic in the scenes was recomputed (market total 2,20 + 3,60 + 0,90 + 1,80 = 8,50 ✓; the 50-euro budget holds ✓).

validator.result: FAIL — 39 rules: 31 pass, 1 fail (LEX-07, 3 blocker in content/course-v2/a1.1/lexicon.json), 2 warn (GRM-04: 4 advisory; LEX-02: 32 ratchet), 5 skipped

verdict: Not exit-ready: 3 BLOCKER (1 in the unit, 2 via the validator's LEX-07 on the shared lexicon), 10 MAJOR, 13 MINOR. The scenes are well made: the prices add up, du/Sie is correct everywhere, the H1/H2 blocks have the right item counts, options, plays and a/b/c and R/F balance, and they are original. What stops exit: one sentence-building key that the German prompt does not determine, a class of sentence-building items that reject correct orders, false Artikel/Stück explanations, a can-do proof that can be solved without German, a butter-price contradiction between the flyer and the announcement, and a can-do (produkt-infos) whose proving Aufgabe never asks it.

findings.quote: promptDe „Bilden Sie den Satz.“ · tiles [Sie / haben / auch Birnen] · answer „Haben Sie auch Birnen?“
findings.problem: The German prompt does not ask for a question. The rendered form is 'Bilden Sie den Satz: [Sie / haben / auch Birnen]', and „Sie haben auch Birnen.“ is a correct German sentence built from these tiles. check.js folds the '?', so a learner who builds the statement is marked WRONG. Only promptEn ('Build the question') determines the key, which ITM-01 forbids.
findings.fix: promptDe „Bilden Sie die Frage.“ (and the same on ls2-p06, ls2-p09, ls3-p07, ls3-p08, whose keys are also questions), or accept „Sie haben auch Birnen.“ with acceptedWhy.
findings.proposedRule: ITM-01/ITM-09: a sentence_building item whose answer ends in '?' must have promptDe naming a question („Bilden Sie die Frage.“); one whose answer ends in '.' must not have a V1 permutation of its tiles (see F04).

findings.quote: LEX-07: „helfen“ (VERB) is entered more than once (a1.2:lx.helfen); „mitkommen“ (VERB) is entered more than once (a1.2:lx.mitkommen)
findings.problem: The validator fails this unit's run because the a1.1 lexicon and the a1.2 lexicon both enter helfen and mitkommen. This does not come from u04's own content, but it makes the u04 validation FAIL.
findings.fix: Lexicon owner: keep each lemma in the level that introduces it first (a1.1) and drop the a1.2 duplicate. Do not rename either one to -2, because they are not homographs.

findings.quote: LEX-07: „halten“ (VERB) is entered more than once (b1.1:lx.halten-2) with different glosses: to stop; to hold | to think of (have an opinion)
findings.problem: halten appears in a1.1 and in b1.1 (as halten-2) with different glosses. LEX-07 requires one gloss per lemma, and a homograph must take the -2 suffix consistently.
findings.fix: Lexicon owner: keep one entry lx.halten ('to stop; to hold') and make the b1.1 sense ('halten von = to think of') a separate lemma or a sense of the same entry, as the SCHEMA lexicon rules require.

findings.path: steps[0].pool.items[4] (ls1-p05), steps[0].pool.items[8] (ls1-p09), steps[2].pool.items[8] (ls3-p09); also ls1-p08, ls1-r03
findings.quote: ls1-p09 tiles [die Milch / auch / ist / billig] accepted only „Die Milch ist auch billig.“ · ls3-p09 [die Butter / auch / ist / dort] lacks „Auch die Butter ist dort.“ · ls1-p05 [ist / der Käse / im Angebot] lacks „Ist der Käse im Angebot?“
findings.problem: Correct orders are rejected. (a) „Auch die Milch ist billig.“ and „Auch die Butter ist dort.“ are the most natural of all orders here, yet neither is accepted, even though ls3-p09 accepts the rarer „Dort ist die Butter auch.“. (b) This unit reviews g.ja-nein-frage and trains it in ls2-p08. With punctuation folded, a V1 order such as „Ist der Käse im Angebot“, „Sind die Äpfel heute billig“ or „Kosten zehn Eier 1,99 Euro“ is a grammatical sentence from the tiles, and 'Bilden Sie den Satz' does not exclude it. (c) Topicalised predicatives („Billig sind die Äpfel heute.“, „Billig ist das Wasser heute.“) are grammatical but not accepted. Object fronting is accepted elsewhere in the unit („Ein Brot brauchen wir heute.“), so the treatment is inconsistent. ITM-09 passes these items, so the gate has a hole.
findings.fix: Add „Auch die Milch ist billig.“ (ls1-p09) and „Auch die Butter ist dort.“ (ls3-p09), and add „Billig sind die Äpfel heute.“ / „Billig ist das Wasser heute.“ with acceptedWhy. For statement keys, either add the final '.' as a fixed tile shown in the builder, or change promptDe to „Bilden Sie einen Aussagesatz.“.
findings.proposedRule: ITM-09: enumerate the permutations of the tiles, including 'auch' + NP in the Vorfeld, fronted predicatives, and the V1 order whenever the tiles contain a finite verb. Every permutation that a German grammar oracle (or reviewerConfirmed) marks grammatical must be accepted or excluded by promptDe.

findings.quote: „Wir brauchen zwei Flaschen Wasser und ___ Brot.“ → explanation „das Brot → ein Brot. Mit der und das: ein.“
findings.problem: The explanation states a rule for the nominative inside an accusative frame (brauchen + object), so it teaches ✗„Wir brauchen ein Käse / ein Apfel“, which the rule card rc.akkusativ has to unteach two units later. The spec also declares g.akkusativ as this unit's chunk preview, and curriculum/a1-1.md §4 prescribes the fixed phrase „Ich möchte einen Kaffee / einen Apfel“. Yet no learner-visible line, redemittel or item contains „einen“ (it occurs only in TTS 'say' fields: „einen Euro achtzig“). Meanwhile the writing task (lp1 cues „Käse“, „Äpfel“) and the micro-outputs invite masculine singular objects.
findings.fix: ls1-p02 explanation: „das Brot → ein Brot. Brot ist neutral: ein.“ (no der-claim). Add the chunk as the plan says: redemittel „Ich möchte einen Apfel, bitte.“ (function 'um etwas bitten', marked as a fixed phrase), plus one input line that uses it.
findings.proposedRule: GRM-01/GRM-04: a unit that declares grammar.chunk must present that chunk in at least one input line or redemittel. An explanation that states a nominative article rule must not sit on an item whose gap is an accusative object.

findings.quote: „Prospekt: „Angebot! Butter, 250 Gramm: nur 1,19 Euro“. Was kostet die Butter?“ — options 2,50 / 1,90 / 1,19 Euro
findings.problem: The only proof of cd.a1.prospekt-preise can be solved without German: the digits 1,19 appear in the stem and in exactly one option. Nothing in the unit makes the learner find a price in a flyer with several products or compare two ads, although the plan asks for 'zwei Anzeigen vergleichen' and the spec says they 'vergleichen Angebote im Prospekt'. All LS1 input items are tagged hoeren, and their prices are also spoken in the dialogue.
findings.fix: Give q02 a mini-flyer of 3–4 lines (e.g. Butter 250 g 1,19 · Käse 200 g 1,99 · Milch 0,99) and ask „Was kostet die Butter?“ with the other prices as options. Add one lesen input item on the LS1 flyer text (e.g. „Was kostet die Butter im Prospekt?“) that is not in the dialogue.
findings.proposedRule: ITM-01: a choice item fails when its key string (or its digits) appears verbatim in the stem and in no distractor.

findings.quote: cd.a1.produkt-infos: „Ich kann im Geschäft fragen, was etwas kostet, wie viel ich bekomme und wo ich etwas finde, und auf solche Fragen antworten.“
findings.problem: The productive can-do is 'proven' by the Sprechen Teil 3 Aufgabe, but that task only makes requests with picture cards („Ich möchte ein Brot, bitte.“ – „Ja, hier, bitte.“). It never asks for a price, a quantity or a location, and it never answers such questions. Asking where something is („Wo ist der Reis?“) appears only as sentence-building tiles. Answering a price question is never produced. So the can-do is claimed rather than performed.
findings.fix: Either prove produkt-infos with the ls2 spoken micro-output, extended to „Fragen Sie nach dem Preis und fragen Sie, wo etwas ist.“ plus one AI-staff reply to answer, or add a Verkäufer round to the LS5 task after the Sp3 cards, with moves price? / how much? / where?. Keep Sp3 as exam practice for request/reaction.
findings.proposedRule: ALL-02: an Aufgabe that proves a can-do must list moves or Leitpunkte that cover each function verb of the can-do (fragen/antworten/bitten …); a cards-request task can prove only a request can-do.

findings.quote: LS1 flyer „Heute im Angebot! … Butter, 250 Gramm: nur 1,59 Euro“ · LS3 announcement in the same supermarket „Und die Butter: 250 Gramm für 1,19 Euro. Nur heute!“ · q02 „Prospekt: … Butter, 250 Gramm: nur 1,19 Euro“
findings.problem: On the same Saturday, the same supermarket's 'today only' butter offer costs 1,59 € in the flyer and 1,19 € in the announcement, and the proof item quotes the flyer at 1,19 €. A learner who read LS1 carefully gets a contradiction from the proof item.
findings.fix: Make it 1,19 € everywhere (flyer line „Butter, 250 Gramm: nur 1,19 Euro“) or keep 1,59 € and change ls3-l02 and q02 to match.

findings.quote: „Arjun: „Zehn Stück, bitte.“ Was kauft er?“ — explanation „Stück sagt man bei Eiern, nicht bei Reis oder Wasser.“
findings.problem: The explanation is false and contradicts LS2, where „Drei Stück, bitte.“ refers to pears. Stück is used with any counted item (Brötchen, Birnen, Äpfel, even bottles in speech). Arjun never says „Zehn Stück, bitte“ in the input, so the only cue is world knowledge, and „zehn Flaschen Wasser“ is a defensible reading.
findings.fix: Stem: „Die Durchsage: „Eier! Zehn Stück kosten nur 1,99 Euro.“ Was ist im Angebot?“ (options zehn Eier / zehn Kilo Reis / zehn Flaschen Wasser). Explanation: „Stück sagt man bei Sachen, die man zählt: Eier, Birnen, Brötchen. Reis kauft man in Kilo.“

findings.path: steps[3].texts t2, t6 (sd1.h1) and t8, t9 (sd1.h2); scripts/course-v2/rules/TXT-02.mjs
findings.quote: sd1.h1 textWords [32, 53] = „±15 % of the 6 sample dialogues (38–46 words)“ · t2 27 words, t6 29 · sd1.h2 textWords [29, 47] = „±15 % of the 4 sample texts (34–41)“ · t8 27, t9 27
findings.problem: Four of the ten exam texts are shorter than the official-sample band in the lane registry. TXT-02 still passes them because it applies a second ±15 % on top of textWords, which already contains the ±15 % (h1 becomes 27–61, h2 becomes 24–55). The whole H1 set averages about 33 words against official samples of 38–46, so the Teil trains on easier-than-exam texts without being flagged as scaffolded for length.
findings.fix: Lengthen t2 and t6 to ≥ 32 words (e.g. a greeting and a thank-you turn, or a distractor quantity) and t8 and t9 to ≥ 29 words. Rule-smith: remove the second tolerance in TXT-02, or store the raw sample range in the registry and apply ±15 % once.
findings.proposedRule: TXT-02: when a template's textWordsSource says the band already includes the tolerance, compare against textWords directly (TOLERANCE = 0).

findings.quote: „Das Angebot ist nur heute.“ / „Das Angebot ist nur heute!“
findings.problem: This is unidiomatic on two listening model surfaces (one of them an exam text). A shop assistant or announcer says „Das Angebot gilt nur heute.“ or „Das gibt es nur heute.“. With 'ist', the sentence reads like a calque of 'The offer is only today'.
findings.fix: „Das Angebot gibt es nur heute.“ (all words known), or simply „Nur heute!“ as in ls3-l02.

findings.quote: promptDe „Bilden Sie den Satz.“ / promptEn „Build the question.“
findings.problem: These four items have question keys but a German prompt that asks for 'den Satz'. Only the English gloss says 'question', which ITM-01 forbids as the only cue. No correct statement order can be built from these tiles, so they are not wrong keys like F01. But the German frame misdescribes the task, and the pattern produced the F01 blocker.
findings.fix: „Bilden Sie die Frage.“ on all four (SCHEMA's own example a2.1-u07-ls3-p06 does this).

findings.quote: cd.a1.preise: „Ich kann Preise und Mengen verstehen und zur Kontrolle deutlich wiederholen.“
findings.problem: The second half of the can-do, repeating a price aloud to check it, is never rehearsed. No micro-output, read-aloud or model turn has a learner echo a price („1,99? Gut.“), and the proof q01 tests only understanding.
findings.fix: Change the LS1 read-aloud to a price echo („Eins neunundneunzig? – Ja, 1,99 Euro.“), or add to the ls2 spoken micro-output: „Wiederholen Sie den Preis.“ after an AI stallholder reply.

findings.quote: partner: „Haben Sie Äpfel?“ · hintWords „Haben Sie …?“
findings.problem: In Sprechen Teil 3, an information question in place of a request is sent back (sd1.json sp3 source). A bare „Haben Sie Äpfel?“ is a yes/no information question and is the weakest request form to model. The learner's own model turns correctly use „Ich möchte …, bitte.“
findings.fix: Model the partner request as „Ich möchte bitte Äpfel.“ or „Haben Sie Äpfel für mich?“, and make the hint „Haben Sie … für mich?“.

findings.quote: lp1 „Was brauchen Sie? Nennen Sie zwei oder drei Sachen.“ · lp2 „Wie viel brauchen Sie?“ · checklist „du-Form“ · model ends „Viele Grüße“
findings.problem: (a) lp1 and lp2 overlap: one noun phrase („ein Kilo Äpfel“) satisfies both. SD1 Schreiben Teil 2 Leitpunkte are three separate content points, each scored on its own. (b) The checklist requires a 'du-Form', but nothing in the task needs one and the model text has none. (c) The model's Gruß has no name.
findings.fix:
Make lp2 distinct, e.g. „Wann sind Sie zu Hause?“ or „Fragen Sie: Ist der Käse im Angebot?“ (keeping lp3 the price question), and put the quantity into lp1 („Was und wie viel?“). Either drop 'du-Form' or make lp3 require it („Fragen Sie Arjun: Was kostet …? / Hast du …?“). End the model with „Viele Grüße
Sam“ (or the learner-name slot).

findings.quote: „Priya sagt: „Die ist teuer.“ Was ist teuer?“ → die Milch
findings.problem: In the input, Priya says „Die Milch ist auch billig, oder?“ and Arjun confirms 99 Cent. Keying 'die Milch' to 'teuer' contradicts the scene the item cites.
findings.fix: „Priya sagt: „Die ist billig.“ Was ist billig?“ with options der Käse / die Milch / die Äpfel (the key is still die Milch, by die + ist).

findings.quote: Start „nur noch ein Ei“ vs t3 „Wir haben nur noch zwei Eier.“ · ls3-l10 „wir haben noch Geld für morgen!“ · t9 „Morgen ist der Supermarkt wieder von 8 bis 20 Uhr offen.“
findings.problem: The unit is framed as 'Samstagmorgen', yet 'morgen' (Sunday) shopping and a supermarket reopening tomorrow go against the plan's own Landeskunde point, „sonntags meist geschlossen“. The egg count also shifts between the Folge and the exam scene with the same couple. The planned Landeskunde (Pfand, sonntags geschlossen, bar oder Karte) appears nowhere, and fokus[] is empty.
findings.fix: ls3-l10 „Und wir haben noch Geld für die Woche!“. t9: „Heute ist der Supermarkt nur bis 18 Uhr offen. Am Montag ist er wieder von 8 bis 20 Uhr offen.“ (or keep it as a weekday text with no link to the Saturday). t3: „nur noch ein Ei“. Add one line of Landeskunde (e.g. „Sonntags sind die Geschäfte zu.“) to the cliffhanger or the LS3 end line.

findings.quote: „Priya, schau mal!“ · „ab sofort frei“ · options „beim Reis“ / „bei der Milch“ / „beim Wasser“
findings.problem: Receptive look-aheads without gloss: the du-imperative (g.imperativ-du-ihr, receptive from a1.2-u09), „ab sofort“, and dative 'bei/beim' as answer options one unit before its chunk (g.praep-dativ chunkFrom a1.1-u05). All are receptive, so this is not a ceiling breach, but they are unglossed.
findings.fix: Cliffhanger „Priya, hier! Eine Wohnung!“ (or gloss „schau mal“ = 'look'). Gloss „ab sofort“ ('from now on'). For ls3-i04, options „dort bei der Milch“ are fine, or gloss „bei = next to“.

findings.quote: „Wie viel kosten die Brötchen für Priya?“ · h1-04 distractor „2,20 Euro“ · h2-04 „Wurst und Käse sind heute im Angebot.“
findings.problem: h1-01's stem is awkward German („kosten … für Priya“). h1-04's distractor 2,20 € is never heard in t4, unlike SD1 practice, where all three options are usually mentioned. h2-04 repeats the text's two nouns plus „im Angebot“ and is answerable by word-spotting.
findings.fix: h1-01 „Wie viel bezahlt Priya?“ (or „Was kosten zehn Brötchen?“). h1-04: make one heard price the distractor (e.g. a banana price for 'ein halbes Kilo'), or keep 2,40 and add „1,20 € ein Kilo, 2,40 € zwei Kilo“ to t4. h2-04: test a detail („Der Käse kostet heute 1,49 Euro.“ → falsch).

findings.quote: ls1-mo „Arjun ist im Supermarkt. Er schreibt: „Was brauchen wir?“ … Was brauchen Sie?“ · ls6 „Arjun ist jetzt im Supermarkt. Sie brauchen auch etwas.“
findings.problem: Two of the three written productions are the same scene (Arjun in the supermarket, you tell him what to buy), which is bland. ls1-mo also answers „Was brauchen wir?“ with „Was brauchen Sie?“, and it sets Arjun in the supermarket while LS1 has him at home with the flyer.
findings.fix: ls1-mo: „Priya fragt: „Was brauchen wir?“ Schreiben Sie die Einkaufsliste in 1–2 Sätzen: Wir brauchen …“ (at home, from the flyer). Keep the supermarket message only for LS6.

findings.path: glosses of token „Kunden“ in steps[2].input, texts t7, t9, t10
findings.quote: { token: „Kunden“, gloss: { en: „customer“ } }
findings.problem: The token is the plural („Liebe Kunden“), but the gloss is singular.
findings.fix: gloss en „customers (sg. der Kunde)“.
findings.proposedRule: Gloss rule: when a glossed token is a plural form of the lemma, the gloss is plural or names the singular.

findings.quote: „Auf der letzten Seite steht eine Anzeige: „2 Zimmer, Küche, Bad – in Leipzig, ab sofort frei.““ · „Fünfzig Euro für alles?“
findings.problem: Flat ads do not usually appear in a supermarket's own Prospekt. They would be in the free Wochenblatt or a Kleinanzeigen page. Also, a couple with a Blue Card software developer on 50 € for a whole week's groceries is a stretch that the text never motivates.
findings.fix: „In der Zeitung steht eine Anzeige …“ (gloss Zeitung if not yet known), or „Am Schwarzen Brett im Supermarkt hängt ein Zettel …“ with a gloss. Motivate the budget in one line („Bis Montag haben wir nur fünfzig Euro im Portemonnaie.“), or say it is only the market-and-offers money.

findings.quote: „Ich möchte ein Kilo die Tomaten.“ / „Wir brauchen 500 Gramm der Käse.“ → errorTag „gender-article“
findings.problem: The planted error is an article after a quantity (Nullartikel), not a gender error. Tagging it gender-article sends a learner who misses it to the wrong repair card.
findings.fix: Tag it as a quantity/Nullartikel error. If ErrorTag has no value for this, record it for the rule-smith, because the enum lacks the class the spine point g.artikel-genus-plural names ('Nullartikel bei Mengen').
findings.proposedRule: SCHEMA ErrorTag: add 'null-article' (or similar) so that g.artikel-genus-plural's third sub-rule has a repair target.

findings.quote: det.adjektiv-endung-unbestimmt on „bisschen“; det.adjektiv-endung-nullartikel on „möchten“; det.trennbare-verben on „Was macht das zusammen?“ / „Das macht zusammen 8,50“
findings.problem: All four GRM-04 advisories are false positives. „ein bisschen“ is an indefinite pronoun, not an adjective ending. „möchten“ is the unit's own spine verb. In „Das macht zusammen …“, 'zusammen' is an adverb, not the separable prefix of zusammenmachen. There is no ceiling breach in the unit, but the heuristics will fire on every shopping unit.
findings.fix: No unit change. Rule-smith: add „bisschen“ and the möchte paradigm to the detectors' stoplists, and exempt „macht (das) zusammen“ / „kostet zusammen“ from det.trennbare-verben.
findings.proposedRule: Detector fixtures: 'ein bisschen', 'Sie möchten', 'Das macht zusammen 5 Euro' must not fire.

findings.quote: „Brot“ recurs in 0 later unit(s) (need ≥ 2) … „Supermarkt“ recurs in 0 later unit(s)
findings.problem: This is expected at this stage: u04 is the only authored a1.1 unit on disk, so no later unit can recycle the 32 new lemmas yet. It is not a unit defect, but it must be re-measured at the level round.
findings.fix: None now. Later units' authors should recycle at least Brot, Käse, Milch, Wasser, Apfel, Kilo, Flasche, Euro, kosten, kaufen, brauchen, billig, teuer (the plan's productive anchors), e.g. in u05 (Wohnung/Anzeige prices), u07 (Öffnungszeiten) and u09 (Essen, bestellen, bezahlen).

findings.quote: „Arjun sagt: „Wir brauchen ein Ei.“ Wie viele Eier?“ — options ein Ei / zwei Eier / zehn Eier
findings.problem: The item is trivial because the key is copied from the stem, and it does not do structured-input work on Genus or Plural. It also uses the plural „Eier“ in the question before any plural input has been shown.
findings.fix: „Arjun sagt: „Die Eier sind billig.“ Wie viele Eier sind das?“ with options „ein Ei“ / „mehr als ein Ei“ / „kein Ei“, which forces the learner to read 'die … sind' as plural.

exitCheck.note: Exit needs 0 BLOCKER / 0 MAJOR / every criterion ≥ 4 / ≤ 5 logged MINOR. F02/F03 belong to the lexicon owner, not the u04 author. F04, F05, F10, F12, F23 and F24 are class findings for the rule-smith.
